newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares up in summer lull after U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares up in summer lull after U.S. gains.

text.p: Swedish shares opened firmer on Wednesday after Wall Street closed at a second consecutive record high overnight but trade was light in the summer lull.
The Stockholm general index was 0.61 percent higher at 3,167.33 at 0815 GMT after shares worth 357 million crowns changed hands.
"There are a lot of American and British buyers in the market at the moment and this is pointing the bourse in a positive direction," one broker said.
U.S./Swedish drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn edged up 0.5 to 298.5 crowns.
It posted lower than expected profits for the second quarter of 1997 on Tuesday with earnings per share of $0.34 against expectations of $0.36 and warnings that the negative trends were continuing.
"It is surprising that the report was not even worse," said one broker. "The restructuring and savings programme for the next year is looking good and I think the share could rise a bit today."
Fellow drugs company Astra rose two to 148.5.
The other market heavyweight, telecoms Ericsson, gained six to 360 crowns. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
